response.sql: WITH filtered_fees AS (SELECT f.*, o.dealedge FROM fees f INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate > 0.0009), group_stats AS (SELECT orderslink, dealedge, AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS group_avg_net_fee, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM filtered_fees GROUP BY orderslink, dealedge), side_averages AS (SELECT dealedge, AVG(group_avg_net_fee) AS side_avg_net_fee FROM group_stats GROUP BY dealedge), filtered_groups AS (SELECT gs.orderslink, gs.dealedge, gs.group_avg_net_fee, gs.record_count, gs.group_avg_net_fee - sa.side_avg_net_fee AS difference FROM group_stats gs JOIN side_averages sa ON gs.dealedge = sa.dealedge WHERE gs.group_avg_net_fee > sa.side_avg_net_fee) SELECT orderslink, dealedge, group_avg_net_fee, record_count, difference FROM filtered_groups ORDER BY difference DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: When computing average net fee rate via AVG(feerate - rebrate), NULL rebrate values cause the expression to evaluate to NULL and are excluded from the average, following SQL's standard NULL handling for arithmetic expressions.

alternatives.interpretation: NULL rebate values should be treated as zero (no rebate received), so the average net fee rate is computed as AVG(feerate - COALESCE(rebrate, 0)). This includes all records in the group average, substituting 0 for missing rebates.
